intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that MEHMO syndrome (MEHMO) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the EIF2S3 gene on chromosome Xp22.11.

paragraphs.text: MEHMO syndrome is a rare X-linked intellectual disability syndrome. Its name is an acronym of its main features: mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity (Steinmuller et al., 1998; Skopkova et al., 2017). In severely affected males, early-onset insulin-dependent diabetes, profound developmental delay, and death in early childhood have been reported. Skopkova et al. (2017) proposed that more severe EIF2S3 mutations cause the full MEHMO phenotype, while less deleterious mutations cause a milder form with only some of the features. Gregory et al. (2019) described a milder phenotype with hypopituitarism and glucose dysregulation caused by an EIF2S3 missense mutation.

paragraphs.text: Delozier-Blanchet et al. (1989) described 2 brothers with severe postnatal growth retardation and severe mental retardation. Other features were extreme microcephaly, obesity that developed during infancy, microgonadism, and a characteristic amphora-shaped face. The neurologic examination was highly abnormal, showing hypertonia, hyperreflexia, nystagmus, and extremely irritable and agitated behavior. The first child died at 4.5 years; he also had neonatal hypoglycemia and chronic constipation. The authors noted a resemblance to Borjeson-Forssman-Lehmann syndrome. However, the dwarfism and mental retardation in their patients were much more severe, and the neurologic and dysmorphic features differed. They suggested a new disorder with recessive inheritance, either autosomal or X-linked. Skopkova et al. (2017) did not find EIF2S3 variants in the index patient of this family (see HETEROGENEITY).

paragraphs.text: Leshinsky-Silver et al. (2002) reported a child with MEHMO and lactic acidosis. A muscle biopsy showed markedly reduced activities of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes 1, 3, and 4. Histologic staining showed mitochondrial proliferation and lipid storage. Electron microscopy showed abnormal, enlarged mitochondria with concentric cristae and electron-dense bodies. The authors proposed that MEHMO is an X-linked mitochondrial disorder. Skopkova et al. (2017) later found that this patient, who was of Ethiopian Jewish origin, carried a SERAC1 mutation and no EIF2S3 variant (see HETEROGENEITY).

paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) studied 3 affected males from a family of Moroccan Jewish ancestry in the maternal line; the grandparents were first cousins. Features included moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphism. Each affected individual also had features of his own: cleft lip and palate and behavioral impairment in one, generalized seizures in another, and postpubertal microgenitalism and obesity in the third. Brain MRI showed a thin corpus callosum and enlarged lateral ventricles. Skopkova et al. (2017) noted that one of these patients could speak in short sentences and feed himself, and that the patients were able to walk, with an ataxic gait.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) reported 4 families with MEHMO syndrome; family 3 was the family originally reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998). The proband of family 1 was born to nonconsanguineous Slovak parents. Microcephaly was diagnosed prenatally at 28 weeks' gestation. At birth his length was 47 cm (-2.0 SD) and his occipitofrontal circumference (OFC) was 32 cm (-2.6 SD), and he had micropenis, cryptorchidism, and peripheral hypertonia. Partial complex seizures began at 4 months and were resistant to anticonvulsants. He had severe mental and motor delay and central obesity, with a BMI of +3.7 SD at 2 years. Dysmorphic features were full cheeks, large ears, downturned corners of the mouth, epiblepharon, long eyelashes, thick eyebrows, tapered fingers, and talipes. Brain MRI showed delayed myelination, and at 19 months it also showed acute demyelinating changes and cerebral atrophy. Non-autoimmune diabetes mellitus was diagnosed at 10 months and treated with insulin. During repeated respiratory infections his seizures worsened and his diabetes control deteriorated. Muscle biopsy at 17 months showed abnormal muscle and mitochondria, and complex II activity was decreased while complex IV activity was normal. At 5 years his height was 88 cm (-5 SD) and his head circumference 39 cm (-8.4 SD). He reacted only to strong tactile stimuli. Neonatal hypoglycemia and panhypopituitarism were also recorded.

paragraphs.text: Gregory et al. (2019) studied 3 affected males from a nonconsanguineous white European family: monozygotic twin brothers and their maternal cousin. They had severe recurrent hypoglycemia and short stature with growth hormone and TSH deficiencies. Their glucose levels fluctuated between hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and postprandial hyperglycemia. Later, the twins had elevated HbA1c and impaired glucose tolerance. The twins had a microphallus, hypoglycemic seizures at 2 years of age, and central hypothyroidism from 2 years. They nevertheless progressed through puberty spontaneously. Brain MRI showed variable white matter loss and a small anterior pituitary in all 3 boys. The cousin also had hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and asymmetric ventricles. None of the boys had severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, epilepsy, or obesity. They had mild learning difficulties and attended mainstream school. Gregory et al. (2019) considered this phenotype distinct from classic MEHMO syndrome.

paragraphs.text: In 3 related males with hypopituitarism (growth hormone and TSH deficiencies), glucose dysregulation, and mild learning difficulties, Gregory et al. (2019) identified a hemizygous c.1294C-T transition in the EIF2S3 gene, resulting in a pro432-to-ser (P432S) substitution at a highly conserved residue in the C-terminal domain of eIF2-gamma. The patients were monozygotic twin brothers and their maternal cousin from a nonconsanguineous white European family. The mutation was found by X-chromosome exome sequencing. It was inherited from the heterozygous mothers and was absent from the ExAC and gnomAD databases. In yeast, the corresponding mutation increased GCN4-lacZ expression about 1.7-fold. It also raised UUG-initiated reporter expression from about 1.6% to 3% of AUG-initiated expression, indicating a modest impairment of eIF2 function.

checks.claim: Gregory et al. (2019) studied 3 related males with hypopituitarism (growth hormone and TSH deficiencies), glucose dysregulation, and mild learning difficulties.
checks.evidence_quote: three related males with normal head circumferences and mild learning difficulties, hypopituitarism (GH and TSH deficiencies), and an unusual form of glucose dysregulation
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The 3 related males studied by Gregory et al. (2019) carried a hemizygous c.1294C-T transition in the EIF2S3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a novel hemizygous variant in EIF2S3 (ENST00000253039.8): ChrX_24091319 C/T, c.1294C > T, p.Pro432Ser (GRCh37) in all 3 affected males
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 c.1294C-T transition results in a pro432-to-ser (P432S) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: c.1294C > T, p.Pro432Ser (GRCh37) in all 3 affected males
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 P432S substitution affects a highly conserved residue in the C-terminal domain of eIF2-gamma.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant is located at a highly conserved residue in the C-terminal domain of eIF2γ across multiple species
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The 3 males with the EIF2S3 P432S mutation were monozygotic twin brothers and their maternal cousin.
checks.evidence_quote: Three affected males, monozygotic (identical) twin brothers (III4, III5) and their maternal cousin (III3)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The family with the EIF2S3 P432S mutation was a nonconsanguineous white European family.
checks.evidence_quote: A non-consanguineous white European pedigree with three affected male patients
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 P432S mutation was found by X-chromosome exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing of the X-chromosome revealed a novel missense variant c.1294C > T in EIF2S3 (p.Pro432Ser)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 P432S mutation was inherited from the heterozygous mothers.
checks.evidence_quote: in all 3 affected males, inherited from their heterozygous mothers (sisters)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 P432S mutation was absent from the ExAC and gnomAD databases.
checks.evidence_quote: The EIF2S3 c.1294C > T, p.Pro432Ser variant was absent from control databases including the Exome Aggregation Consortium (ExAC) (www.exac.broadinstitute.org) and the Genome Aggregation Database 2018 (gnomAD)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: In yeast, the mutation corresponding to EIF2S3 P432S increased GCN4-lacZ expression about 1.7-fold.
checks.evidence_quote: The p.P490S mutation resulted in a modest, but statistically significant, ~1.7-fold increase in GCN-lacZ expression
checks.explanation: P490S is the yeast equivalent of P432S.

checks.claim: In yeast, the mutation corresponding to EIF2S3 P432S raised UUG-initiated reporter expression from about 1.6% to 3% of AUG-initiated expression.
checks.evidence_quote: In eIF2γ WT, the HIS4(UUG)-lacZ reporter was expressed at ~1.6% the level observed with the canonical HIS4(AUG)-lacZ reporter
checks.explanation: The text goes on to say that P490S raised this to 3% of the AUG-initiated value.

checks.claim: The yeast results indicate that the EIF2S3 P432S mutation modestly impairs eIF2 function.
checks.evidence_quote: Cumulatively, our results demonstrate that the human p.Pro432Ser eIF2γ modestly impairs eIF2 function
checks.explanation: Stated directly.
